claims.text: Reducing the drug/cyclodextrin training dataset size from 3000 to 500 samples increased the mean absolute error from 1.38 to 2.28 kJ/mol.
Reducing the drug/cyclodextrin training dataset size from 3000 to 500 samples decreased the R2 value from 0.86 to 0.58.
A random forest model trained on 646 solid dispersion formulations achieved a prediction accuracy of 82.5% for stability prediction.
A LightGBM model trained on 3000 drug/cyclodextrin formulations achieved an R2 value of 0.86 on the test set.
Deep learning models achieved over 80% accuracy in predicting the disintegration time of orally fast-disintegrating films.
The FormulationDT machine learning framework achieved an average ROC_AUC score above 0.90 across 12 classification models for drug formulation strategy design.
Partial least squares regression using molecular surface descriptors predicted intrinsic aqueous drug solubility with an R2 of 0.91.
The Rule of Five (Ro5) principles define essential technical criteria for building reliable artificial intelligence formulation prediction models.

evidence.description: Reducing the dataset from 3000 to 500 samples led to substantial performance degradation, with mean absolute error (MAE) increasing from 1.38 to 2.28 kJ/mol.
Reducing the dataset from 3000 to 500 samples resulted in R2 decreasing from 0.86 to 0.58.
Comparative evaluation of eight machine learning algorithms revealed that the random forest model achieved the highest prediction accuracy of 82.5% on the test set for a dataset of 646 formulations.
Among three algorithms evaluated on a dataset of 3000 formulations, the LightGBM model performed best, achieving an R2 value of 0.86 on the test set.
Deep learning achieved over 80% accuracy in predicting the disintegration time of orally fast-disintegrating films.
FormulationDT covers multiple decision-making steps with a total of 12 machine learning classification models, achieving an average ROC_AUC score above 0.90.
PLS analysis establishing correlations between molecular descriptors and intrinsic solubility of 17 compounds yielded a predictive model with an R2 of 0.91.

The Ro5 includes criteria: formulation dataset containing at least 500 entries, coverage of minimum 10 drugs and all significant excipients, appropriate molecular representations, inclusion of critical process parameters, and suitable algorithms with model interpretability.

methodologies.name: Rule of Five (Ro5) Guidelines for Formulation Prediction
methodologies.description: A set of five standardization guidelines established to direct researchers in building reliable AI models for drug formulation prediction.
conditions: Coverage of >= 10 drugs and critical excipients

limitations.text: Early AI models relied on small datasets (<100 samples) and basic molecular descriptors, leading to poor generalization and inability to capture complex drug-excipient interactions.
Deep learning models act as black boxes, making their automatically learned representations challenging to interpret.
Large language models are prone to hallucinations, generating plausible but factually incorrect information that poses risks in pharmaceutical R&D.
Quantum mechanics and molecular dynamics simulations are computationally demanding and restricted to short time scales.

future_work.text: Expanding large language model applications across the drug delivery pipeline from literature extraction and formulation design to regulatory review.
Deeply integrating AI with multiscale physical and biological modeling techniques, including AI-PBPK and AI-QM/MD hybrid frameworks.
Developing self-driving AI laboratories (AI-SDLs) to autonomously design, execute, and optimize formulation experiments.
